fact: The Lagoon Nebula, a star-forming region in Sagittarius, about 4,100 light-years away.
bio: Giovanni Battista Hodierna discovered it in 1654. It can be seen with the naked eye in a dark sky. Its young cluster NGC 6530 is only a few million years old. A Gaia study suggests that the cloud's collision with the plane of the Galaxy, about 4 million years ago, may have set off most of the star formation. The Hourglass region holds twisting funnels half a light-year long.
